facts.statement: The genus name Abrosaurus means 'delicate lizard' in Greek.
facts.quote: Abrosaurus (; 'delicate lizard' from the Greek meaning 'delicate' or 'dainty' and meaning 'lizard')

facts.statement: Abrosaurus was a relatively small sauropod, reaching a maximum length of 9.1 meters.
facts.quote: It was rather small for a sauropod, measuring no more than 9.1 m long.

facts.statement: Abrosaurus had a boxy head topped with a tall bony arch that housed its nostrils.
facts.quote: Its head was boxy and topped with a tall, bony arch containing the nostrils.

facts.statement: The skull of Abrosaurus featured large openings separated by thin bony struts, which inspired its name.
facts.quote: The generic name refers to the nature of the skull, with large openings separated by thin, bony struts.

facts.statement: Abrosaurus was discovered in 1984 and first described in a 1986 doctoral thesis by Chinese paleontologist Ouyang Hui.
facts.quote: Abrosaurus was discovered in 1984 and was first described in the 1986 Ph.D. thesis of Chinese paleontologist Ouyang Hui

facts.statement: Ouyang Hui formally described the species in 1989, initially naming it Abrosaurus dongpoensis.
facts.quote: Ouyang formally described this species in 1989 under the specific epithet A. dongpoensis.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Abrosaurus is a nearly complete and well-preserved fossil skull designated ZDM 5038.
facts.quote: The holotype, or original specimen, of Abrosaurus, ZDM 5038, is a fossil skull which is nearly complete and very well preserved.

facts.statement: All known fossil material of Abrosaurus originates from the Dashanpu Quarry near Zigong, China.
facts.quote: All of the material comes from the famous Dashanpu Quarry near Zigong in China

facts.statement: Abrosaurus lived during the Middle Jurassic Period, approximately 168 to 161 million years ago.
facts.quote: These sediments are dated from the Bathonian to Callovian stages of the Middle Jurassic Period, or about 168 to 161 million years ago.

facts.statement: Abrosaurus was a quadrupedal herbivore.
facts.quote: Like most sauropods, Abrosaurus was a quadrupedal herbivore.

facts.statement: While originally classified as a camarasaurid, research suggests Abrosaurus is a basal member of Macronaria.
facts.quote: Abrosaurus was originally described as a camarasaurid sauropod, and while it may not turn out to be a member of that particular family, further research has indicated that it is a basal member of Macronaria

facts.statement: Abrosaurus was originally described as a camarasaurid sauropod but is now considered a basal member of Macronaria.
facts.quote: Abrosaurus fue descrito originalmente como un saurópodo camarasáurido, y mientras que puede no resultar ser un miembro de esa familia en particular, la investigación posterior ha indicado que es un miembro basal de Macronaria, como el propio Camarasaurus.

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database lists the parent group of Abrosaurus as Mamenchisauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Mamenchisauridae

facts.statement: Abrosaurus fossils are housed in a museum in Zigong.
facts.quote: Fue encontrado en la famosa mina de Dashanpu, Zigong donde se halla en un museo.

facts.statement: Abrosaurus is characterized by a delicate skull with large openings separated by thin bone bars that housed large nasal openings on top.
facts.quote: Este saurópodo se caracteriza por tener un cráneo delicado con grandes fenestras separadas por delicadas barras de huesos, que en vida albergarían grandes fosas nasales en la parte superior del cráneo

facts.statement: Abrosaurus is considered a small sauropod genus, reaching about 9 meters in length, 3 meters in height, and weighing around 10 tons.
facts.quote: Dentro de los saurópodos, puede ser considerado como un género pequeño, de solo 9 metros de largo, 3 de alto y unas 10 toneladas de peso.

facts.statement: The species name 'dongpoi' honors the Chinese poet Su Shi, also known as Su Dongpo, who was born in Sichuan.
facts.quote: El nombre de especie, dongpoi, se debe al poeta chino Su Shi del , también conocido como Su Dongpo, que nació en Sichuan.

facts.statement: The name was corrected from Abrosaurus dongpoensis to Abrosaurus dongpoi in 1999 by Peng & Shu to follow biological nomenclature rules for male individuals.
facts.quote: Finalmente, Ouyang describió formalmente la especie en 1989, bajo el epíteto de especie de A. dongpoensis, pero, y según los parámetros de la nomenclatura biológica, el sufijo latino -ensis debería ser reemplazado por -i para los nombres masculinos, lo cual fue enmendado por Peng & Shu en 1999 quienes le dieron el nombre de Abrosaurus dongpoi, que es el considerado como válido.

facts.statement: The exact placement of Abrosaurus in the sauropod family tree remains difficult to determine because its remains have not been fully described.
facts.quote: However, the remains of Abrosaurus have not been fully described, making its exact placement in the sauropod family tree difficult to determine.

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database records the time range of Abrosaurus as the Bajocian to Oxfordian stages, from 170.9 to 154.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Bajocian to Oxfordian (170.9 to 154.8 million years ago)
